pr_title: roachtest: VM hostError should be flagged as an infra flake
pr_body:
Previously, we were seeing roachtest failures due to `compute.instances.hostError`. These were being wrongly directed to different engineering teams while in reality the VM hostError is an infra flake.

This PR flags the `compute.instances.hostError` as an infra flake and avoids the unnecessary noise.

Epic: none
Fixes: #101223
Release note: None

issue_context.title: roachtest: VM hostError should be flagged as an infra flake
issue_context.body:
In theory, VM hostErrors are infrequent [1]. In practice, we see them at least once a month during triage. E.g., a recent roachtest failure was a result of `compute.instances.hostError` [2]. However, the root cause was only determined after examining roachtest logs/artifacts. To reduce this type of noise, roachtest can automatically perform a post-mortem (e.g., by querying a cloud API) and report an infrastructure flake if a hostError was observed in the cluster under test (failure).

[1] https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/faq#hosterror
[2] https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/100998

Jira issue: CRDB-26870
comments:
In GCE, `compute.instances.hostError` is written to the system (audit) log. We can easily parse out the necessary info, post-mortem, e.g.,

```
gcloud beta --project cockroach-ephemeral logging read "resource.type=gce_instance AND protoPayload.methodName=compute.instances.hostError AND logName=projects/cockroach-ephemeral/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Fsystem_event" --format json --freshness=30d |jq '.[] | "\(.receiveTimestamp),\(.protoPayload.resourceName)"'
```
